title: cognitive function in patients with heart failure or aortic valve stenosis
summary: Patients with heart failure are at an increased risk of developing dementia. A general principle applies here: the risk of dementia increases as the severity of the heart failure increases. In particular, episodes of cardiac decompensation lead to a transient worsening of heart failure. This phenomenon is reproducible in mouse models, suggesting that the correlation between heart failure and cognitive dysfunction is not attributable to confounding factors—such as a globally elevated cardiovascular risk—but rather that a direct link appears to exist between heart failure and cognitive function. Through this study, we aim to gain a better understanding of this relationship in order to facilitate future therapeutic interventions. This study is designed as an observational cohort study comprising two subgroups. Group 1 consists of patients with heart failure who are admitted due to cardiac decompensation. Group 2 consists of patients with aortic valve stenosis scheduled for a TAVI procedure. In both groups, cognitive and cardiac function will be assessed over a longitudinal course, thereby enabling us to draw conclusions regarding the relationship between cardiac function and cognitive function.
conditions: Other specified degenerative diseases of nervous system

interventions.name:
Clinical Cohort Study: Patients with heart failure or aortic valve stenosis undergo simultaneous cardiac and neuropsychological assessments. In addition to routine data, the following measures are collected: the 6-minute walk test, the KCCQ questionnaire, and neuropsychological testing.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
heart failure or aortic valve stenosis
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent from the patient or caregiver
Age <18 years or >90 years
Malignant tumor disease
History of stroke with significant residual deficits
Severe respiratory insufficiency (requiring NIV for >4 hours)
Acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, pulmonary embolism
Systolic blood pressure <100 mmHg
